title: Debugging, regression checks and reproducible scripts
outcome: Reduce a defect to a small case and build behavioral checks that cover ordinary, boundary and rejected inputs.
mechanism:
Debugging begins by making the failure reproducible. Preserve the exact input, observed result and intended behavior before changing several things at once. A minimal example removes unrelated data and dependencies while retaining the failing mechanism. In a classroom pad, a self-contained script also avoids hidden session state from an earlier run.

Inspect structure as well as printed values. str, typeof, length and dim can reveal a dropped dimension or unintended coercion that rounded console output hides. Add assertions near the boundary where an invariant first becomes necessary. A later nonsensical model result may originate in an earlier ID join, missingness mask or vector-length mismatch.

A regression test should exercise behavior, not simply repeat the implementation's formula. For a weighted mean, check a deliberately unequal group-size example whose expected result is derived independently. Include an empty population, a missing or invalid weight and a zero-total-weight case under the declared policy. Catching every error and returning success would invalidate the test.

Reproducibility also includes random-number configuration and package versions. set.seed establishes a repeatable stream for a chosen generator configuration; it does not make different algorithms or arbitrary future package versions identical. sessionInfo records useful environment context. Avoid asserting that one fixed numerical sequence must match across every R version, platform and package change without a supported compatibility contract.

vocabulary.definition: A small self-contained input and program that retains a defect.
A property expected to hold throughout an operation.
A check that prevents a known defect from returning.
Inputs, configuration and version evidence needed to interpret a result.

anatomy: Use stopifnot for compact behavioral assertions and isTRUE(all.equal(...)) for a justified numeric tolerance. Test an expected error with a narrow handler. Reset the seed immediately before a reproducibility comparison and retain source plus session metadata.

worked_examples.title: A behaviorally specified weighted mean
worked_examples.code:
weighted_average <- function(x, w) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(x), is.numeric(w), length(x) == length(w), length(x) > 0L)
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(x)), all(is.finite(w)), all(w >= 0), sum(w) > 0)
  sum(x * w) / sum(w)
}
stopifnot(weighted_average(c(10, 20), c(1, 3)) == 17.5)
stopifnot(weighted_average(c(10, 20), c(2, 6)) == 17.5)
print(weighted_average(c(10, 20), c(1, 3)))
worked_examples.explanation: The independent expected amount is \((10+60)/4=17.5\). Scaling every weight by the same positive constant is a useful invariant that tests meaning rather than source text.

worked_examples.title: Repeat a seeded stream deliberately
worked_examples.code:
set.seed(17)
first <- runif(4)
set.seed(17)
second <- runif(4)
stopifnot(identical(first, second))
stopifnot(all(first >= 0 & first <= 1))
print(list(same_stream = identical(first, second), r_version = getRversion()))
worked_examples.explanation: Resetting the same seed before each draw reproduces this generator stream in the same environment. The range assertion checks a separate distribution-support property.
worked_examples.expected: The two vectors match exactly in this run.

exercises.prompt: Derive the weighted mean of 10 and 20 with weights 1 and 3.
exercises.hint: The denominator is total weight, not number of values.

exercises.prompt: Add tests for mismatched lengths and zero total weight.

exercises.hint: The same mistake can appear on both sides.

exercises.expected: Add independently derived fixtures and invariants.

exercises.prompt: Repeat a random draw under the same seed.
exercises.answer: The vectors match within the declared environment/generator configuration.
exercises.expected: The vectors match within the declared environment/generator configuration.

exercises.prompt: Write a useful bug report for a dropped matrix dimension.
exercises.hint: Include minimal source, shape before/after and the required contract.
exercises.answer: A reviewer can reproduce the failure without the original private data or hidden session.
exercises.expected: A reviewer can reproduce the failure without the original private data or hidden session.

reference:
weighted_average <- function(x, w) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(x), is.numeric(w), length(x) == length(w), length(x) > 0L)
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(x)), all(is.finite(w)), all(w >= 0), sum(w) > 0)
  sum(x * w) / sum(w)
}
stopifnot(weighted_average(c(10, 20), c(1, 3)) == 17.5)
stopifnot(weighted_average(c(10, 20), c(5, 15)) == 17.5)
rejected <- function(x, w) tryCatch(
  {
    weighted_average(x, w); FALSE
  },
  error = function(e) TRUE
)
stopifnot(rejected(c(10, 20), 1), rejected(c(10, 20), c(0, 0)), rejected(numeric(0), numeric(0)))
stopifnot(rejected(c(10, NA_real_), c(1, 1)))
set.seed(17); first <- runif(4)
set.seed(17); second <- runif(4)
stopifnot(identical(first, second), all(first >= 0 & first <= 1))
cat("r-020 reference checks passed\n")
